\[
\gamma(u, v) = \frac{\sum_{x, y} \big(I(u + x, v + y) - \bar I_{u,v}\big)\big(T(x, y) - \bar T\big)}{\sqrt{\sum_{x, y} \big(I(u + x, v + y) - \bar I_{u,v}\big)^2 \sum_{x, y} \big(T(x, y) - \bar T\big)^2}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(T, \bar T\): The template and its mean
- \(I, \bar I_{u,v}\): The image and the mean of the window at (u, v)
- \(\gamma\): The normalized cross-correlation, from -1 to 1

T is the template, the luma inside the rectangle around the selection, with its mean T bar. For every position (u, v), the window of the image with the same size has the mean I bar. The plain matched filter is the numerator alone, the correlation of the image with the template less its mean. Turin showed that this filter is best for finding a known signal in white noise. But it grows with the contrast of the window, so a faint copy of the pattern scores low and the edge of a bright area can score high. The normalized cross-correlation gamma divides by the spread of the window and of the template. It goes from -1 to 1. It is 1 where the window is the template up to brightness and contrast, and -1 where it is the template with dark and light swapped. A window with no spread gives 0.
